previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain, and leg swelling, with hypoxemia and hypercarbia. Evaluation revealed an exacerbation of diastolic heart failure and obstructive lung disease, worsened by medication non-adherence and opioid use. She developed respiratory acidosis with metabolic compensation, requiring careful oxygen management. Cellulitis of the left leg was treated with antibiotics, and her urinary retention and constipation were managed supportively. Depression and anxiety were addressed with continued medications and outpatient referral. She improved with diuresis, bronchodilators, and infection treatment, and was discharged home with updated medication instructions, smoking cessation support, and follow-up plans.

# Pneumonia: patient presented meeting criteria for sepsis with 
pneumonia as likely source, leukocytosis, fevers, tachycardia 
and respiratory rate on admission, but this resolved her first 
night in hospital. CXR for new cough inconclusive given habitus; 
but given clinical picture was treated for pneumonia. Received 
two days of azithromycin/ceftriaxone, and was discharged on 
azithromycin alone for 5 day course given multiple allergies 
(cefuroxime listed) and hemodynamic stabilty.  Other sources of 
infection that were considered were c. diff given report of 
diarrhea and multiple risk factors (hospitalization, PPI), but 
patient did not stool to send sample while here; recurrent 
cellulitis was also considered but patient felt leg had been 
improving since last hospitalization. She was instructed to seek 
medical attention if her symptoms worsen or do not improve ta 
home. 

# Leukocytosis: Most likely related to infectious etiology as 
discussed above. Not on steroids on admisison to raise suspicion 
for demarginalization. No clear cause for stress response 
either. Resolved after one day of antibiotics. 

# Anemia: Presented with normocytic anemia to hematocrit of 35, 
baseline appears to be 38-40. No obvious source of bleeding, but 
she is having diarrhea (does not appear to be bloody or like 
melena per pateint). Dilutional also possible from  IVF in the 
ED. Otherwise nutritional deficiencies or hemolysis could also 
be considered given elevated TBili (mostly indirect). Further 
inpatient work up not persued as total bilirubin normalized the 
next day and hematocrit was stable. 

# Elevated Tbili and alk phos: Has had similar cholestatic 
picture in the past; no focal signs of gall bladder pathology on 
exam, and alk phos is only slightly elevated on admission, 
normalized the following day. Interestingly bili fractionated 
out to only 25% conjugated, possibly indicative of intermittent 
hemolysis as discussed above.

# COPD exacerbation: Increased wheezing and dyspnea as well as 
cough possibly triggered by HCAP as discussed above.  Per last
